items.descZh: llmspeed 是一款针对本地大语言模型（LLM）推理性能的开源模拟工具，旨在帮助用户在实际购买硬件前，直观评估不同设备与模型组合的运行效率。其核心功能是允许用户自由组合硬件（如 NVIDIA RTX 5090、Mac Studio M5 Ultra、AMD RX 7900 XTX 等）与主流模型（如 Qwen、Llama、DeepSeek 等），基于社区验证的基准测试数据，模拟出 tokens/sec（每秒生成 token 数）和 time to first token（首 token 响应时间）等关键性能指标。该工具的亮点在于其数据源自 r/LocalLLaMA 等社区的真实 benchmark，提供高度可信的本地推理速度预测，且完全免费开源。它非常适合个人开发者、AI 爱好者以及企业采购人员，在构建本地 AI 工作站、升级 Mac 或 GPU 设备，以及对比云端实例（如 H100）与本地部署性价比时做出高效的决策。
items.quote: 在购买前先挑选硬件和模型，亲身体验本地 LLM 的真实速度。

items.title: Show HN: Gittins, an online bandit engine that enforces log correctness
items.desc: description: Gittins is an opinionated, highly optimised contextual bandit engine. title: Gittins – Productiongrade contextual bandits image: https://www.getgittins.dev/gittinsog.png Contents Principles Gittins is an opinionated, highly optimised contextual bandit engine that aims to address the practical considerations with such systems, based on my experience working with bandit problems. It stands on the shoulders of giants, in particular [Vowpal Wabbit](https://vowpalwabbit.org), and adheres strictly to a design in support of realworld production use. Gittins is not a research tool. 1. 1. Online by nature Gittins learns one observation at a time, in O(1) work, and in fixed memory as long as open decisions are regularly resolved. 2. 2. Nonstationarity is expected For many realworld problems, the relationship between context and feedback drifts over time. A contextual bandit engine must learn to adapt over time, and never learn something it cannot eventually unlearn. 3. 3. Dynamic actions and context If you want to choose what banner to display on your website, and the set changes each day, an engine must accept this, and clean up after itself. There should never be a case where you must specify the number of actions beforehand. 4. 4. Simple algorithms, bringyourown models The builtin algorithms should be readable by any competent programmer, and work in practice. Sophistication lives in the layering and the API, not in any single component. Users can swap in their own prediction model and/or exploration algorithm, and inherit everything else. 5. 5. Safe reward handling Rewards in bandits may arrive late, or not at all. Constructing invalid training data from logs or external sources must be nigh on impossible by design, not merely discouraged. 6. 6. Speed and determinism Fast decision cycles allow for unexpected use cases. Gittins must have bestinclass single core performance, and rely on few to zero dependencies. Bitidentical results across platforms and language bindings must be guaranteed and enforced by a golden test corpus. Code changes must be validated by tens of thousands of simulations and a large test battery. 7. 7. Multislot and large action sets Many problems are ranking / multiposition problems; therefore problems with thousands of candidate actions must be practical, fast, and robust. 8. 8. Offline policy evaluation It must be possible to estimate how a new policy would have performed using only logged decisions from an old policy. 9. 9. Choose your own complexity The same model needs to be able to run (a) ephemerally in memory, (b) persisted to a flat file, or (c) used via a shared service. There should be no need for databases; indeed, the model weights should be possible to check in to version control and deploy as part of normal deployment workflows. These concepts are discussed throughout this document, which serves both as an introduction to bandits and as technical documentation for Gittins. I encourage the reader to read the whole document once; once you have understood the concepts on a broad level, use the contents above to jump to sections you need to reference. The contextual bandit problem In the contextual bandit setting, you (repeatedly): 1. Observe a context 2. Choose an action 3. Receive a reward for the action you chose The objective is to learn to select the best action for any given context such that you maximise total reward over time. From this problem setting, it follows that contextual bandit algorithms must try out different actions to learn what context/action pairs lead to the best rewards; they must _explore_ the action space using some exploration algorithm, and also _exploit_ their knowledge using some learned model. Some bandit algorithms explore first, then exploit. Some learn to explore less over time, converging at some point on the optimal action for a given context. Gittins uses a simple algorithm known as epsilongreedy, where exploration always happens for a small portion of decisions, regardless of how long the bandit has been running. This is a deliberate choice to tackle nonstationarity, an issue I revisit later in this document. It is also a practical choice: epsilongreedy is surprisingly hard to beat in practice. The simulation below runs the real engine in your browser on a small problem: two contexts, three actions, and a different best action for each context. Watch the bandit start at random and settle on the right banner per device, while still exploring a small share of the time. Loading the gittins engine… You may be thinking to yourself, "why not use supervised learning instead of bandits?". That is a fair question, and for some problems, it works well. But consider a case of topic recommendation on social media. If you use supervised learning to choose the best topic from a handful of candidates, you must a) have enough cover in your training data to learn the optimal relationships, however obscure, and b) have some way of being able to recommend entirely new topics that you don't have history for. Bandits offer a natural way of introducing new actions by virtue of its explorative design. Your first decision Gittins comes in three flavours: a (slow) reference Python implementation, which is not packaged and not recommended outside development of the system; Python bindings, for most data science workflows; and WASM bindings, for inbrowser decisions. The bindings call a core written in Rust for performance reasons. Whichever flavour you pick, the interface is the same eight functions with the same names and the same semantics. A state saved by one loads in the others, bit for bit. The examples on this page default to Python; use the toggle above any code block to switch to the WASM (JavaScript) API, and the whole page follows. All you need resides in one module, gittins. There is no schema to define, nothing to register, and no background machinery. Start by creating a bandit. What you get back is a handle: decide, learn,
items.author: maxpagels
items.descZh: Gittins 是一个面向生产环境的上下文多臂老虎机引擎，旨在解决实际系统中的非平稳性和动态动作集等挑战。它采用在线学习模式，每次决策仅需 O(1) 计算资源并保持固定内存，确保高效运行。引擎支持数千候选动作的多槽位排序，并具备位一致的跨平台确定性，通过数万次模拟和严格测试保障可靠性。用户可替换内置的探索算法和预测模型，同时享受安全的奖励处理机制，防止无效数据污染。此外，Gittins 提供离线策略评估功能，并允许模型以内存、文件或共享服务形式部署，无需数据库，便于版本控制和持续集成。适用于需要实时适应变化的推荐系统、广告投放等生产场景。

items.descZh: Aethel Core 是一款以后端仿真为核心的 Web 应用防火墙，其核心防护逻辑完全基于 Prolog 语言编写，目前系统处于被动防御状态且已成功接入 Shield 保护。该产品的突出亮点在于其纯 Prolog 实现的 137k 条句法规则，构成了极难被攻破的逻辑迷宫，目前在 Hackme 挑战中仍无人能成功绕过。它适用于对安全性有极端要求的后端系统，通过形式化逻辑而非传统签名库来识别和阻断攻击行为。Aethel Core 代表了一种将编程语言特性转化为安全防御优势的创新思路。

items.author: pulkitbanta
items.descZh: 该工具专为解决本地开发MCP（模型上下文协议）服务器时，前端UI与后端服务并行迭代的配置痛点而生。其核心功能是提供一种简化的本地测试环境，使开发者无需依赖复杂的Docker重定向即可高效处理顶层 `/.well-known` URL 的访问需求。最大的亮点在于避免了每次UI或后端调整后都必须重建容器应用的繁琐步骤，实现了无缝的本地实时联调。该工具非常适合需要频繁进行MCP协议本地调试、追求高效迭代周期的开发团队和个人开发者使用。
items.quote: 我在本地开发 MCP 服务器时构建了这个工具，因为我希望同时开发 UI 和后端服务器，并不断对其进行迭代。

items.descZh: 针对社区中大量开发者对 PyTorch 张量操作练习的迫切需求，作者推出了名为 Tensor Golf 的专项训练平台，旨在帮助用户建立处理张量运算的信心与流畅度。该平台核心功能是提供系统化的张量操纵练习，通过实战导向的互动挑战加深用户对 PyTorch 基础语法的理解。其核心亮点在于通过针对性的训练，显著提升用户在张量变形、索引和 broadcasting 等核心操作上的处理效率与准确率。该工具非常适合深度学习初学者、算法工程师以及需要提升代码底层性能的科研人员，用于日常技能打磨与实战演练。
items.quote: 我收到了很多关于张量操作练习的请求，所以我想创建一个地方，帮助大家建立使用 PyTorch 的信心并提高熟练度。
